target_customer: Accredited investors who want exposure to YC startups (Demo Day Access Fund) and, later, founders partnering with its AI venture studio
problem: Individuals cannot easily invest in YC companies at seed stage; the firm packages diversified YC batch exposure, later also builds its own AI companies.
business_model: Fund management (fees and carry on access funds) plus a venture studio that builds and holds AI SaaS companies
product_category: Venture fund and AI venture studio

founders.name: Kaushik Tiwari
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he has worked in digital health, insurtech, fintech and AI; no employers named.

founders.name: Saumik Tiwari
founders.background_notes: YC bio mentions Dorm Room Fund involvement and building financial products.

competitors.name: AngelList Demo Day Funds
competitors.what: Alumni-led funds raised before each YC cycle offering accredited investors exposure to a YC batch
competitors.traction_then: Not stated; current page says funds are raised before each cycle

technical_complexity.rationale: A fund vehicle and newsletter need legal structuring, not hard engineering; the later studio builds standard AI SaaS products.

defensibility.rationale: Access to YC deal flow is not exclusive; the firm itself states it has no formal YC relationship via its disclaimers and many alumni funds do the same.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: AngelList and alumni funds continued offering Demo Day Funds; no one acquired or displaced Attack Capital in sources found.

market_need_then: Retail and accredited investors lacked access to YC seed deals; YC itself publishes an investment policy limiting who can invest around Demo Day. Evidence of demand at the time is thin in sources found.

branding.domain_note: Uses attack.capital as a domain hack; legal entity is Better Financial Corporation DBA Attack.

identity.voice_and_tone: Fast, aggressive startup positioning: only YC alumni founded AI venture studio built to move with speed

branding.brand_signature: Termsheet by Attack Capital newsletter on Substack
branding.community_and_virality: Weekly Substack newsletter on Series A startups and secondary markets; the Term Sheet name overlaps with Fortune's Term Sheet newsletter.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct name and a content channel, but little independent press on the brand itself.

pivots.to: AI venture studio building its own vertical AI companies
pivots.why: Third party profile (superscout) says the firm moved to full incubation; reason not stated

outcome_analysis: Attack Capital began in 2022 as a fund giving accredited investors diversified exposure to YC batches and shifted in January 2024 to an AI venture studio that spins out companies such as PowerDialer and HealOS. It is still operating with a small team. Fund size, fees and returns are not public, so success or failure cannot be judged from available sources.
notes: No funding rounds found for the management company; its own funds are not company rounds. The AngelList source is dated well after founding (current page), so the competitor entry is flagged: AngelList Demo Day Funds existed as an offering but its start date was not verified. Founder bios come only from the YC page. Stage of the pivot comes from a single profile source.
